title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up the transcendental (analytic) description of elliptic curves and of their families. This prepares an analytic construction of the modular stack / Teichmüller-type covering, which the following page carries out.

(1) Over C, an elliptic curve E is equivalent to a pair:
 (a) a rank-2 free Z-module H = π1(E,0_E) ≅ H_1(E,Z) = H^1(E,Z)^∨;
 (b) a complex structure on V = H⊗_Z R. This V is identified with t_E = Lie(E), the tangent space at the origin, via the universal cover.

(2) Then E ≅ (H⊗R)/H as a real Lie group (a 2-torus). The complex structure on V descends to the quotient, so (a)+(b) recover E as a complex Lie group.

Relative version over a complex-analytic base S:
- (a) becomes a local system ℋ of free Z-modules of rank 2, namely R^1f_*Z dual, or equivalently the relative H_1. It yields the real-analytic vector bundle ℋ⊗_Z R.
- (b) becomes a structure of complex line bundle on ℋ⊗R, i.e. an identification with Lie(E/S). It must make the local sections of ℋ holomorphic.
- In modern terms this is a polarizable variation of Z-Hodge structure of weight −1, rank 2, type {(−1,0),(0,−1)}. The holomorphy condition is the holomorphicity of the period map; Griffiths transversality is automatic in this case.

The next page continues:
- Choose sections z1, z2 of ℋ forming a real basis fibrewise. The complex structure is then encoded by τ = z2/z1 ∈ O_S(S), with τ(s) ∈ C∖R.
- A 'structure de Torelli' is a trivialization t: Z_S^2 ≅ ℋ.
- Elliptic curves with Torelli structure form a rigid category. The fine moduli space is presumably C∖R (both half-planes, since no orientation is fixed), and the modular stack is the quotient by GL(2,Z).

The content is the classical Weierstrass/Riemann period description of elliptic curves and its family version.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor imprecision: 'les sections locales de ℋ deviennent des sections analytiques complexes' should be read as: the image of ℋ in the complex line bundle (≅ Lie(E/S)) consists of holomorphic sections, i.e. ℋ⊗O_S → Lie(E/S) is an O_S-linear surjection. This is the standard Hodge-filtration condition, and it is clearly what is meant.

ideas.what: Elliptic curve over C equals lattice H plus complex structure on H⊗R; E ≅ (H⊗R)/H
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of complex tori / Hodge structure of weight −1 of rank 2

ideas.what: Relative version: local system ℋ of rank 2 plus complex line-bundle structure on ℋ⊗R making sections of ℋ holomorphic, encoding a family of elliptic curves over an analytic base
ideas.modern_name: Variation of Hodge structure of weight −1 (rank 2); period map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1960s), Deligne (equivalence of 1-motives/abelian schemes with VHS of type (−1,0),(0,−1))
ideas.where_published: Analogous family descriptions appear in Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II/III

ideas.what: 'Structure de Torelli' = global trivialization of ℋ (full marking of H_1); rigidifies the moduli problem, with period τ ∈ C∖R
ideas.modern_name: Marked elliptic curves / Teichmüller (Torelli) space in genus 1; full level structure on H_1(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Teichmüller space of genus 1 = upper half-plane)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un programme speaks of Teichmüller structures/towers; the specific term 'structure de Torelli' is not known to me in print

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook transcendental description of elliptic curves and their families (the genus-1 period map), written as a preparatory step. The only mildly idiosyncratic feature is the terminology 'structure de Torelli' (marking of H_1) and the deliberate use of both half-planes C∖R. These are standard ideas.
transcription_corrections: Line a): the word in quotes is 'réseau' (somewhat malformed, possibly with a correction), not entirely deleted; it is followed by 'i.e. Z-module libre de rang 2'. The struck fragment at the end looks like '[-E#=1-]' or similar.
In b), a struck symbol after 'H⊗_Z R' precedes '(≃ t_E, espace tangent à l'origine de E)'.
'La donnée a) permet de reconstituer E comme groupe de Lie réel par' is correct; 'et la donnée b) redonne la structure complexe sur E, par passage au quotient' is correct.
'La structure b) correspond : une structure complexe [-sur-] de ce dernier, en tant que fibré vectoriel {+complexe+} [-de-] rang 1' is consistent with the image.
